messages:
Kartik: spotted an old KMS IAM grant that gives `svc-ci@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` Decrypt on key `backups-prod-key`. Looks like it was left after migrating CI in 2022.
Elena: can you paste the binding? we need to know if it's key-level or keyring-level.
Kartik: policy snippet: `\n{\n  "bindings": [\n    {\n      "role": "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter",\n      "members": ["serviceAccount:svc-ci@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]\n    }\n  ]\n}\n` It's on the key resource, but the key is used for archived backups.
sec-oncall: Action plan: 1) revoke the binding (temporary deny), 2) run decrypt audit export, 3) rotate CI credentials + Vault role, 4) scan backups for matching ciphertext headers.
Kartik: revoked the member via `gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding` and saved the policy diff to /tmp/ci-kms-diff.json.
Maya: nice. before rotation: capture logs for last 90 days for Decrypt calls. DevBot: /run gcloud logging read 'resource.type="kms_crypto_key" protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:svc-ci@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com' --freshness=90d --format=json > /tmp/ci-decrypts.json
Elena: check if any third-party integrations (pager, partner webhooks, analytics) reference svc-ci SA. If so rotate those secrets too.
ops-ci: scanning helm values and k8s serviceaccounts now. Found three helm releases `ci-runner`, `ci-artifacts`, `legacy-backups` referencing the old SA in annotations.
sec-oncall: Treat `legacy-backups` as high-risk because it wrote long-lived blobs to gs://backups-prod-archive. Queue immediate quarantine.
Kartik: started a gsutil inventory and checksum collection for objects under gs://backups-prod-archive/2022/**. Running in dry-run to avoid accidental decrypt.
Maya: Vault role `secret/roles/ci-agent` also had allowed_kms_keys pointing to that key. We need to update that role to the new key and issue fresh wrapped keys.
Elena: suggest we move to short-lived asymmetric keys for signing and use Workload Identity for CI - reduces need for decrypt privileges.
sec-oncall: Agreed. Immediate mitigation: rebind Vault role to new key `ci-ephemeral-key-v2`, issue tokens TTL=30m, and rotate client certs. Post-mitigation: design migration to asymmetric flow.
DevBot: Reminder posted: /runbook sec/ci-kms-incident v1.2 (https://redwood.internal/runbooks/ci-kms-incident)
ops-ci: Canary patch prepared: update helm values to use `workloadIdentity` and `serviceAccount:ci-wi` then rollout to `ci-runner` on nodepool canary-1.
Kartik: after revocation, logs show 7 Decrypt calls in the last 180d from svc-ci. Pulling more context now (IP, caller service).
Maya: Also check partner SFTP backups, one partner used agent SA to upload archives years ago. If they still do, rotate their upload token and notify partner security.
Elena: Good catch. Also enable long-term audit export for KMS decrypts: create a logs sink to sec-audit-bucket with filter for Decrypt calls and grant write permission to the security audit SA.
sec-oncall: Command to create sink: `gcloud logging sinks create kms-decrypt-sink gs://sec-audit-bucket --log-filter='resource.type="kms_crypto_key" AND protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt"'` then `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding REDWOOD_PROJECT --member='serviceAccount:...@gcp-sa-logging.iam.gserviceaccount.com' --role='roles/storage.objectCreator'`
Kartik: scan found two archived blobs with matching ciphertext headers. Marked them for quarantine and hash-collection. Copy job started to gs://sec-quarantine/ci-2022-archives/.
ops-ci: started rotation PRs for helm charts. Will coordinate with DevOps to avoid simultaneous deploys. Targeting a 15m window per release.
Maya: after new tokens issued we should run a secret-cache purge for Redwood Optimize caches that may contain wrapped key blobs. I can run the cache invalidation job.
Elena: checklist for post-containment: 1) timeline of events, 2) list of rotated principals, 3) artifacts quarantined, 4) audit export created, 5) recommended RBAC change (narrow to key and move to asymmetric).
sec-oncall: If any external transfer detected, escalate to SecOps lead and open an incident. For now treat as unconfirmed leak.
Kartik: I'll attach the diffs and gsutil inventory to the incident ticket in ~30m. Thanks for the quick responses.
Elena: thumbs up. Keep this thread for updates only.
